title: Security-Agents Integration - December 2025

patterns_identified.name: Agentic AI in Security Operations
patterns_identified.description: 74-75% of enterprises now use AI-driven threat detection and response as core cybersecurity. Autonomous security agents triage alerts, detect malware, investigate incidents, and remediate threats.
evidence: Google Cloud: Agents independently investigate alerts, reverse engineer malware
CrowdStrike: AI agents for endpoint detection and response
Palo Alto Networks: Agentic threat intelligence and automated remediation
Response times reduced from hours to minutes
patterns_identified.expected_impact: Leverage existing security agents for automated code scanning, vulnerability monitoring, incident response

patterns_identified.name: New AI-Specific Threat Vectors
patterns_identified.description: 60% of AI attacks in Q4 2025 aimed to leak system prompts or manipulate agent behavior. New vulnerabilities: prompt injection, system prompt leakage, model poisoning, token compromise.
evidence: Lakera Q4 2025 report: 60% of attacks target system prompts
99% of organizations report at least one AI system attack
Prompt injection now top attack vector for agents
Behavioral manipulation and impersonation attacks emerging
patterns_identified.mitigation_needed: Input validation, service account key rotation, behavioral monitoring, secure inter-agent communication

patterns_identified.name: Agent-Specific Identity Management
patterns_identified.description: Traditional IAM systems insufficient for autonomous agents. Agent-specific identities with unique, auditable credentials replacing shared service accounts (identity flattening anti-pattern).
evidence: Microsoft Entra agent credential frameworks
OAuth 2.0 extensions for agent delegation
Authenticated, authorized, auditable action chains
Real-time credential revocation capabilities
patterns_identified.expected_impact: Per-agent GCP service accounts enable precise tracking and control

patterns_identified.name: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications
patterns_identified.description: Industry benchmark published December 2025 for securing autonomous agents. Covers prompt injection, permission escalation, audit trails, agent-to-agent communication security.
evidence: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (Dec 2025)
10 key risks: prompt injection, system prompt leakage, excessive permissions, inadequate audit trails, etc.
Becoming compliance baseline for agent systems
Complementary to ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF
patterns_identified.action_required: Conduct OWASP Top 10 security assessment of Chained agents

patterns_identified.name: Agent Governance Frameworks Required
patterns_identified.description: ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, GDPR AI-specific requirements now mandate agent governance. Organizations must demonstrate control over agent operations, especially for sensitive data.
evidence: ISO 42001: AI Management System mandatory controls
NIST AI RMF: US federal guidance for AI systems
GDPR: AI-specific data processing requirements
MITRE ATLAS: Adversarial threat landscape for AI
EU AI Act: Risk classification for AI systems
patterns_identified.compliance_gap: Chained needs formal documentation of agent governance, enhanced audit trails, compliance mapping

integration_opportunities.description: Define what each of 8 Chained agents can and cannot access
integration_opportunities.expected_benefit: Prevent identity flattening, enable precise access control

integration_opportunities.description: Create service account per agent, implement IAM with least privilege
integration_opportunities.expected_benefit: Enable precise tracking, prevent lateral movement attacks

integration_opportunities.description: Integrate CodeQL, dependency scanning, security incident detection
integration_opportunities.expected_benefit: 90% faster vulnerability detection, automated incident response

chained_specific_insights.current_state: 8 autonomous agents on GCP Cloud Run, security agents exist (secure-specialist, guardian-master, secure-ninja, monitor-champion), no formal permission policies or per-agent identities
chained_specific_insights.opportunity: At intersection of 'security FOR agents' and 'agents FOR security' - can both secure agent system AND use agents for security operations
chained_specific_insights.governance_gap: No formal agent permission policies, shared service accounts (identity flattening), basic audit trails need enhancement
chained_specific_insights.competitive_advantage: Lead by example with 'security-first autonomous agents' and public transparency about governance
chained_specific_insights.integration_feasibility: HIGH - 15-20 days total effort across 3 phases

key_quotes: 2025 is the year autonomous agents moved from experimentation to production. With that shift came urgent need for security governance.
Chained needs both 'security FOR agents' (governance, permissions, monitoring) AND 'agents FOR security' (automated scanning, incident response).
Most autonomous agent systems have weak security governance. Chained can lead by example.
The future of autonomous agents depends on security governance. Chained has the opportunity to lead, not follow.
